newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ATHLETICS-U.S. ATHLETES LIVE UP TO EXPECTATIONS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-U.S. ATHLETES LIVE UP TO EXPECTATIONS.

text.p: American athletes lived up to expectations at the international athletics meeting in Linz on Wednesday and broke two of the year's best times.
Dennis Mitchell and the U.S. 4x100m team beat the Santa Monica Track Club, with nine-times Olympic champion Carl Lewis, by clocking the year's fastest time of 37.96.
The year's best was previously held by Lewis and his team mates in 38.31, posted only two days ago in Stockholm.
Olympic and world champion Allen Johnson confirmed his good form before next month's world championships in Athens, with the year's best of 13.12 in the 110m hurdles.
Slovakia's Igor Kovac had previously bettered the year's time with 13.30 in Stockholm.
"I'm pretty happy with my performance today, but there is still a lot I can improve on before on before Athens. In Athens, I feel my chance is just as good as anyone else's," said Johnson.
Johnson will participate at the Stuttgart meeting on Saturday before returning home to prepare for the championships.
Mitchell's relay victory was to remain his best result of the day. In the 100 metres, the American posted 10.07 and bowed to compatriot Vincent Henderson, who clocked 10.06.

Henderson will not be competing in Athens as he was injured during the U.S. trials and so did not qualify. "I had a poor start but after 40 metres I found my rhythm and was able to catch up with Mitchell," he said.
Three-times Olympic and world champion Gail Devers had little trouble claiming the women's 100 metres in 11.06 ahead of Nigeria's Christy Opara-Thompson and Debbie Ferguson of the Bahamas.
Cuban long jumper Ivan Pedroso continued his good form before the championships, winning ahead of American Robert Howard with a jump of 8.56 metres.
In the men's javelin, Germany's Boris Henry became only the fifth man ever to exceed the 90 metres mark when he achieved 90.44 to win ahead of Russia's Sergey Makarov (88.54).
Local heroine Theresia Kiesl, an 800 metres Olympic bronze medallist, delighted crowds at Linz by posting the year's best in the mile race, when she clocked 4:25.05.
